criteria: `parse_ini(text)` is implemented in `ini.py` and returns a `dict` that maps each section name to a `dict` of its keys and values, where all names and values are `str`.
`ini.py` does not use `configparser`.
In `parse_ini`, lines end at `"\n"`, and a `"\r"` before the `"\n"` is dropped.
In `parse_ini`, a line that is empty or only whitespace is skipped, and a line whose first non-whitespace character is `;` or `#` is a comment and is skipped.

In `parse_ini`, `[name]` on a line of its own starts a section; whitespace around the brackets and inside them is trimmed (`[ db ]` is the section `db`); section names are case-sensitive; and an empty name (`[]`) is an error.

In `parse_ini`, `key = value` sets a key in the current section: the line is split at the first `=`, key and value are trimmed, keys are lower-cased while values are kept as written, an empty value is allowed (`key =`), and an empty key is an error.
In `parse_ini`, `;` and `#` start a comment only at the start of a line: in `url = http://x/#top ; note` the value is `http://x/#top ; note`.
In `parse_ini`, keys that come before any section header go into the section named `""`, and that section is in the result only when it has at least one key.

In `parse_ini`, a line that starts with a space or a tab, and is not blank or a comment, continues the value of the key before it by appending its trimmed text after one `"\n"`; a continuation with no key before it in the same section is an error; and a section header ends the reach of a continuation.
In `parse_ini`, when the same key appears twice in a section the last value wins, and when the same section appears twice its keys are merged into one dict with later keys winning.
In `parse_ini`, a section with no keys is in the result with an empty dict.
In `parse_ini`, any other line is an error, and errors raise `ValueError` whose message contains `line N`, where `N` is the 1-based number of the bad line.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
